canonical_topic: Example linear load-vs-temperature model for PJM-West
definition: An illustrative simple linear regression relating afternoon summer load to temperature for one region and hour window.
core_idea: For PJM-West load between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m. on August weekdays, the author fits a linear model where load has a fixed base level plus an increment per degree of temperature above a 72°F threshold.
key_points: The model captures the basic relationship that power demand rises with temperature.
The author explicitly notes the model is not complete at this stage — it still needs error analysis to find where it performs poorly.
relationships: A first-pass model to be refined via error analysis into a more complete forecasting model.
trading_implications: Such a simple temperature-slope model can serve as a first-order proxy for hourly demand sensitivity to weather, useful for sanity-checking more complex forecasts.
caveats: The model is only valid for the specific hour window, month, and day type it was fit on (2-3 p.m., August, weekdays) — it is not a general-purpose load model.
